seed: The study behind the queue task find-out-whether-separating-should-hand-you-text. Two shapes, one capture: (A) separating as it works today, which hands you a picture of every label, and (B) separating that reads the words straight away, reproduced by asking for the words on every one of the nine runs in turn. The walk photographs both and proves what one undo press takes back after each.

steps.note: the capture as it opens: one locked Background picture and nothing else

SHAPE A, what the command does today: nine runs of text are their own layers and every one of them is a PICTURE of a label, called Text 1 to Text 9 because nothing has read the words. Changing any of these words is a second command away, and a person has to know it exists.
ONE undo press takes the whole separation back: nineteen layers and the repaired bitmap go together, and the screenshot is one locked Background again. That is the promise any new shape has to keep.

SHAPE B, what separating would hand you if it read the words itself: the same nine layers, every one of them real text wearing its own words. Nine of nine cleared the bar on this capture. The canvas is meant to look untouched, and the layers list is the whole visible difference: General, Launch at login, Show in menu bar and the rest, instead of Text 1 to Text 9.

Asked for run by run, each reading is its own undo step, so one press takes back ONE label: Save Changes is a picture called Text 9 again and the other eight are still words. Folded into the command it would be one step for the lot, because the separation already lands in a single mutation.
